contract_plain_english: For a Poisson random variable X with rate λ, the preceding bound says that whenever t > λ, the entire upper tail satisfies P{X ≥ t} ≤ e^{−λ}(eλ/t)^t. For an integer k in that right tail, Stirling’s formula gives the one-point mass P{X = k} ≈ e^{−λ}(eλ/k)^k/√(2πk). Thus, at the matching integer threshold, the tail-bound expression has the same exponential profile as the first point mass in the tail and differs only by the factor √(2πk). The source regards that square-root factor as negligible compared with the exponential smallness in k and therefore calls the bound quite sharp. This is a qualitative exponential-scale comparison, not an exact asymptotic formula for the full tail. [PDF pp. 8–9 / printed pp. 19–20, Exercise 2.3.3 equation (2.8) and all of Remark 2.3.4]
